summary: The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This is due to the plugin splicing the attacker-controlled request URI into a PHP expression inside a double-quoted string and evaluating it with eval(). Because PHP interpolates double-quoted strings, a payload of the form {${...}} in the URL path is executed during interpolation, so no quote breakout is required and WordPress' slashing does not mitigate it. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server with a single GET request. The affected conditions ship enabled by default and are evaluated before any logged-in check, so no plugin configuration is needed; the site must have BuddyPress and Paid Memberships Pro active alongside this plugin.
title: CVE-2026-120539 (CVSS 9.8)

summary: An Unrestricted File Upload vulnerability in the admin panel of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1 allows authenticated attackers to upload files with arbitrary content by bypassing weak filename extension validation in add-post.php and change-image.php. Although files are renamed with an image extension upon storage, the lack of MIME type and content validation enables content spoofing, storage of malicious markup, and creates a vector for Remote Code Execution (RCE) with server misconfigurations or secondary Local File Inclusion.
title: CVE-2026-128668 (CVSS 8.8)

summary: The WP Import Export Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Limited Code Injection in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.32 via the 'comment' parameter. This is due to a two-stage shortcode check that evaluates the raw mapping placeholder before data substitution, causing the neutralizer to be skipped when attacker-controlled comment content containing a malicious [wpie_function] shortcode is substituted at runtime. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP callables on the server. Exploitation requires an Administrator to perform the standard Export With Settings For Import followed by a New Import migration workflow, which is a routine operational task; the attacker themselves requires no account or authentication, needing only the ability to submit a pending comment on any comments-open post.
title: CVE-2026-19793 (CVSS 8.8)

summary: The PublishPress Revisions: Duplicate Posts, Submit, Approve and Schedule Content Changes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to permanently force-delete arbitrary trashed posts, pages, and revisions owned by any user, including higher-privileged users. The required nonce is trivially harvested by any Contributor-level user because the static 'revisions-deleted' nonce action is emitted in a redirect header on the init hook before WordPress enforces edit.php's capability check, and once obtained it authorizes deletion of any trashed post or revision on the site.
title: CVE-2026-123086 (CVSS 8.1)

summary: The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with everest_forms_create_forms capabilities, to activate any already-installed inactive plugin on the server by supplying an arbitrary slug, triggering its activation hooks and escalating privileges up to administrator level. Exploitation requires that a site administrator has delegated the everest_forms_create_forms capability to a lower-privileged role via the plugin's Role & Permission feature, and that at least one inactive installed plugin whose main file follows the slug/slug.php naming convention exists on the server.
title: CVE-2026-129220 (CVSS 8.8)

summary: The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to permanently delete any comment they authored anywhere on the site — including regular post comments and lesson comments — along with all replies to those comments authored by any other user, including Administrators and Instructors.
title: CVE-2026-118049 (CVSS 8.1)
